chunks: 3809 - He said: I asked him about a broker who purchases for a fee. Silver money is handed over to him, and it is stipulated to him: whatever you buy, I may take what I wish from it and leave what I wish.
So he goes and buys, then comes with the goods and says: Take what you are satisfied with, and leave what you dislike.
So he said: “There is no harm in that.”

key_terms.السِّمْسَارِ: broker or intermediary conducting the purchase
key_terms.الْمَتَاعِ: the goods or merchandise brought back
key_terms.الْوَرِقُ: silver money or coined currency handed over for purchase
key_terms.بِالْأَجْرِ: for a fee or wage in return for the service
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no objection; it is permissible
key_terms.يُشْتَرَطُ: it is stipulated as a condition in the transaction

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islamic law for a broker to buy goods and let the buyer choose what to accept afterward?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling permitting a brokerage arrangement in which the broker purchases goods for a fee and the client later selects what he wishes to keep and leaves what he does not want. It indicates the permissibility of this commercial practice and reflects flexibility in sale arrangements when agreed conditions are in place.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3809 - He said: I asked Imam (as) about a broker who buys for a fee. Money is handed over to him, and it is stipulated that whatever he buys, the buyer has the option to take what he likes and leave what he dislikes.
The broker then goes and makes the purchase, and upon returning with the goods, he says, "Take what you are satisfied with and leave what you dislike."
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in that."
